stemMd:
The engineer's report lists three successful trials, then devotes twice as much space to a failed one. This imbalance is deliberate: the failure reveals a condition under which the proposed device cannot safely be used, whereas the successes all occurred under similar conditions.

Why does the text mention the space devoted to the failed trial?

options.label: A
options.textMd: To show that the engineer concealed every success.

options.label: B
options.textMd: To criticize the report solely for being too long.

options.label: C
options.textMd: To prove the device fails under all conditions.

options.label: D
options.textMd: To explain why an apparently uneven report can prioritize the most informative evidence.

explanationMd: The failed trial adds information about a boundary that the similar successful trials do not reveal. The passage explains the rationale for giving that evidence disproportionate space.

distractorRationale.b: The explanation defends its distribution of attention.
distractorRationale.a: The report lists the successful trials.
distractorRationale.c: The failure identifies a particular limiting condition.
